answers.how: In 1920x1080 coordinates, the bowling ball has a diameter of ~83.7 px, giving a scale of 0.21 m / 83.7 px = 0.002509 m/px. Around t = 0.5 s (Frame 12), the ball center moves from x = 470.5 px at Frame 10 (t = 0.417 s) to x = 674.0 px at Frame 14 (t = 0.583 s), which is 50.86 px/frame or 1220.6 px/s at 24 fps, corresponding to 3.06 m/s.

Fitting the horizontal ball position across Frames 3 to 27 shows a uniform deceleration of ~0.245 to 0.25 px/frame^2 (velocity decreases from ~50.86 px/frame at Frame 12 to ~47.8 px/frame at Frame 24). At 24 fps and 0.002509 m/px, this acceleration magnitude is 0.25 * 24^2 * 0.002509 = 0.36 m/s^2.

Around t = 1.0 s (Frame 24), the ball center moves from x = 1070 px at Frame 22 (t = 0.917 s) to x = 1261 px at Frame 26 (t = 1.083 s), giving a speed of 47.75 px/frame or 1146 px/s at 24 fps. Multiplying by the scale 0.21 m / 83.7 px gives 2.88 m/s.

At t = 1.0 s (Frame 24), the ball is still rolling along the lane prior to pin impact with the same constant deceleration of ~0.25 px/frame^2 (144 px/s^2), which converts to a magnitude of 0.36 m/s^2 using the scale 0.21 m / 83.7 px.
In 1920x1080 coordinates, the standing bowling pins measure ~121 to 127 px tall (mean ~124 px). Using the ball diameter prior of 0.21 m = 83.7 px, the pin height is 124 * (0.21 / 83.7) = 0.31 m.

In 1920x1080 coordinates, the arched black ball return opening at the right end of the foreground lane hood extends vertically from y = 755 px to y = 860 px (105 px tall). Converting with the scale 0.21 m / 83.7 px gives 105 * 0.002509 = 0.26 m.
